**Framework-vs-statutory note (governs until GAP-02 closes):** because the facility's jurisdiction was not supplied, this matrix is issued on the **14-element framework basis (KB-STD-PSM)** — best-practice program structure, not an asserted statutory obligation. If the facility is confirmed as US-based, the matrix converts to a statutory compliance basis under 29 CFR 1910.119 (KB-REG-US-OSHA) with no structural change; action SA-08 closes this. No jurisdiction-specific law is cited in this document until the jurisdiction is confirmed.

**Covered-process note:** a crude unit is characteristically a candidate covered process, but coverage turns on a documented threshold-quantity determination for a highly hazardous chemical, and none was supplied. Coverage is therefore **[GAP]**, not asserted; action SA-07 closes it. Until then the framework basis above also protects against over-claiming statutory coverage.

This document is de-identified for circulation:

- All accountabilities are **role labels only** (e.g. "Mechanical-Integrity Lead (role)"). No personal names, government IDs, contact details, or addresses appear in this document.
- The re-identification key that maps role labels to individuals is held in a **separate, access-controlled artifact**. It is not part of this document, is not reproduced here, and must never be appended to any circulated copy.
- Injury data is aggregated: **12 recordable injuries this period**, with small categories aggregated and all cells below 5 suppressed, with secondary suppression applied so suppressed cells cannot be back-calculated from totals. No category below 5 individuals is published here.

## 5. Confirmed gap detail — Mechanical integrity (High)

**What is known:** the supplied element review records Mechanical integrity as a **Gap**, banded **High**, with remediation owned by the Mechanical-Integrity Lead (role). This is the only evidence-backed status in the program.

**What is not known:** the extract does not describe *what* the deficiency is — whether it concerns inspection and test currency, deficiency backlog, quality assurance of equipment, procedures for maintaining ongoing integrity, or specific equipment classes within the crude unit. This is recorded as **GAP-04**. No engineering detail is invented here: the remediation plan below therefore opens with a characterization step, and no specific equipment fix is prescribed until that step reports.

**Why this matters at High band:** mechanical integrity is the element that keeps covered-process equipment within its design envelope; a High-banded gap in it on a crude unit is, on its face, a candidate loss-of-containment pathway. Interim risk decisions (SA-03) cannot wait for the full remediation plan.

### Remediation approach — hierarchy of controls (KB-SNIP-HOC)

Every remediation control in this plan is ranked by the hierarchy of controls, and **no gap may be closed on a PPE-only or administrative-only treatment without a documented justification**. Because the deficiency detail is GAP-04, the plan fixes the *control-selection discipline* now and the *specific controls* at SA-03/SA-04:

| HoC rank | Control class | Application to the MI gap |
|---|---|---|
| 1 — Elimination | Remove the deficient condition entirely | Permanent repair or removal from service of any equipment found outside its acceptable limits; decommission redundant deficient equipment rather than maintaining it |
| 2 — Substitution | Replace with a lower-risk alternative | Replace defective components or equipment with items restoring full design integrity, rather than derating around the defect |
| 3 — Engineering controls | Engineered interim safeguards | Where permanent repair must be scheduled: engineered interim measures (e.g. verified derate with hard protective settings, isolation of affected sections) — each documented with its basis and expiry |
| 4 — Administrative controls | Procedures, inspection, surveillance | Restored inspection / test / preventive-maintenance schedule; a deficiency-management procedure with tracked backlog; increased operator surveillance rounds — **acceptable only as a bridge to rank 1–3 controls, never as the end state for a High-banded gap** |
| 5 — PPE | Last resort | Never the sole treatment for this gap; any interim measure relying on PPE alone is flagged for immediate escalation to the Site Leadership Team (role) |

**Escalation rule:** if characterization (SA-02) finds any deficiency for which no rank 1–3 control is practicable in the interim, the shutdown / continued-operation decision for the affected equipment is made explicitly and recorded by the Site Leadership Team (role) — it is not defaulted by inaction.

## Limitations

This document is **decision-support only**. It is not legal advice, and it does not constitute or replace a statutory compliance determination. Statuses reflect only the evidence supplied as at 5 July 2026; [GAP] entries mark information that was not provided, not findings of non-compliance. **A competent person must review this output** — including the covered-process determination, the gap-risk banding, and every remediation control — before it is relied upon or acted on.
